request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now name other people on the sheet as their patrons, and each row shows the patrons and their backing. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What you see on a person's row**
- **Patrons:** the patrons' names, sorted and joined by ", ".
- **Backing:** the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a. It shows 0.00 when there are no patrons. It's worked out in the browser from the same due-total each row already shows, so a hold, a rate change or a claim change updates it straight away.
- **Adding a patron:** a drop-down plus an "Add patron" button. The drop-down leaves out the person themselves and anyone who is already their patron.

**Refusals**
- The server refuses a patron who is the person themselves, is not on the sheet, or is already a patron. A refused request writes nothing and shows `person-patron-error` on the row.
- Because the drop-down already hides those choices, the test's two "refused" cases (Ada naming herself, Ada naming Ben twice) pass by not being offered. The server's own refusal and its error message are never run by the test; they're there for cases like two users adding the same patron at once.
- I changed the shared row-error store (`features/people/personError.tsx`) so the patron error has its own slot. Setting any error on a row clears every error on that row, so the next action on the row also clears the patron error.

**Storage and server**
- New table `person_patron` (migration `V22__person_patron.sql`), one record per person–patron pair.
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons` adds a patron and writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> patron=<patron name>` to the audit file.
- `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/patrons` lists them. The server code is in a new `patron` package.

**Front end:** a new `features/patrons/` folder adds the "Patrons" and "Backing" columns next to "Hold".
